*   **Output:** An A-Buffer containing control points (depth $d$, visibility $v$) for each pixel, and textures storing the first and last hit points of the volume traversal.
Perform an iterative merging process to decimate existing control points.
*   **Time Complexity:** The base pass is $O(N)$ per ray where $N$ is the number of voxels sampled (one sample per voxel).
The merging process adds overhead when the buffer is full, potentially increasing complexity depending on the number of merges required.
*   **Measured Performance:** Not given in the sources.
*   **When to use:** When volumetric visibility is needed for illumination calculations (e.g., multiple scattering, optimized light ray entry) and exact ray tracing is too costly.
*   **When not to use:** When exact visibility is required without approximation, or when the scene has extremely high depth complexity that exceeds the fixed layer limit even after merging.
It builds on the concept of approximate visibility functions using a low number of control points, as shown by Salvi et al. [39, cited in S1, unofficial].
The method is similar to deep shadow maps [52, cited in S1, unofficial] but applies the A-Buffer concept to view-space volumetric visibility rather than shadow occlusion.
